This  REVIEW  is about the Gold Shop on the second floor. I went there with my wife a couple weeks ago to look at gold necklaces. Two gold shops and both had good displays of bracelets and babbles. the lowest price range was One thousand bahts. I did not understand the price symbols. But the bored workers there let us look at a few pieces and it became apparent that the price 10,000 baht plus. Then next lowest category was 20,000 +. think we were the only customers there.The necklace that my wife liked was 19,500 baht. I did not want to pay that much but felt shamed by the contempt that the workers showed me and was kind of manipulated into agreeing to buy it to not lose face. The guy refused to accept my visa card. So I walked to the ATM and withdrew 20,000 baht and paid cash. They made a big big deal out the transaction, insisting on making a photocopy of my Passport like these people are so fond of doing... No courtesy - just took  my money and handed over the piece with the receipt.... today we went back there because the thin gold chain had broken.  Wan still had the receipt and she said maybe they would charge her something to make the repair so I gave her 2,000 baht and I went there with her... two women working there and again no customers. The young woman wai'd to us and my wife showed her the broken necklace and receipt. She weighed the piece for some reason and then another woman came into the shop. the other one patted her down. i.e. she felt her bra, front and back, under the bra strap and her hips and waist. Then this one - ignoring me - again weighed the piece and took out the pieces that Wan was considering. The trip was they would exchange the broken chain for a new necklace. I mentioned that she wanted one with a thicker, stronger chain. So the skinny woman who had been searched wrote out a receipt showing a cost of 1,740 baht for the service. I tried to object that if it was under warranty and being exchanged  we should not have to pay. Wan told me that they said she was not supposed to sleep with the necklace on so they would not honor the warranty.
Fine.
We got the new necklace and I helped fasten the clasp and then Wan gave her 2,000 baht. Then they made us wait and wait and wait and wait.... They of course whipped out the cell phone and punched in numbers and showed us that they would give us 260 baht in change. I am old enough to have learned how to count. Then they had to punch the numbers on their computer and print out some more papers. and Wan had to sign some more copies and then they went back to being bored. and we sat and waited and waited and got fed up and walked to the counter and asked the skinny woman what was the problem. I spoke into the TRANSLATE app on my cell phone and showed it to her. and also I told her in Thai and English that she was wasting our time ,. she ignored me and spoke  gibberish to Wan and went back and punched more numbers on the computer and ignored me. Finally she showed Wan two copies of receipts and had her sign them in two places and tore off the bottom part of each paper and then she went back to her computer and then consulted with the co-worker and then counted out the two thousand bahts and then counted out the 260 in change.
I would have left the 260 baht there if I had known they were going to make us wait and wait so long. No wai, no courtesy, no respect. I have read reviews of other gold shops in Chiang Mai where the customers said the owners were very nice. But at this Lotus Ruamchok they are contemptuous.
